clue.text: There was nothing in her closet but a modest gown!

definitions.text: There was nothing in her closet
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nursery-rhyme old woman who went to the cupboard and found it bare
second meaning: a long, loose, shapeless dress that covers the whole body

explanation.surface: A woman with nothing in her wardrobe except one demure dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a poor wardrobe; one meaning is the rhyme ('the cupboard was bare'), the other a style of dress named after her pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's old woman found her cupboard empty, and the loose all-covering dress shown in her illustrations took her name.

clue.text: Brother setting up the old firm in sharp practice

parts.note: a brother in a religious order

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the archaic spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A monk raising up an old-established company while dealing dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for trickery or underhand, mischievous dealing in place of honest conduct.

clue.text: Reverse call

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the back face of a coin
second meaning: what you shout when a coin is tossed, as opposed to heads

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs (turn back, telephone); each is a coin-tossing noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a coin opposite the monarch's head is its back face, and naming that side is a bet when it is flipped.

clue.text: Cheer the XI, a real smasher!

indicators.note: a smasher breaks things up, so the preceding words are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters taken as written, with XI as two letters

explanation.surface: A fan cheering a cricket eleven on with praise for one great player.
explanation.walkthrough: XI looks like a team of eleven but supplies just its two letters to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone in the sense of making them glad is to elate or enliven them greatly.

clue.text: The lad died in any case!

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation sits within the following word
a case holds something, so the last word wraps around the first

parts.note: taken as written; it forms the outside
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the boy is dead whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' reads as the phrase meaning anyway; split it, and the word any encases the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A common boy's given name serves as an example of a lad, short for Andrew.

clue.text: Attachment warranted to shatter traditions, nothing less

indicators.note: shattering breaks a thing into pieces, so the word is broken and rebuilt
less means without, so that much is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A justified attachment, permitted to break every tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from the ten letters first, then rearrange the remaining nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraint is the legal seizure of goods under a warrant to force payment of a debt, which lawyers also call attachment.

clue.text: Explanation supported by a student of building

parts.note: a construction is an interpretation put on words, as in 'put a kind construction on it'
taken as written
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An account backed up by someone studying architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, being supported by means sitting on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to building or putting structures together.

clue.text: Fellow-resident I try to clean out at cards?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who lives next door to you

parts.words: I try to clean out at cards?
parts.note: setter's reading: a children's card game whose title is 'Beggar my ...', in which you aim to win every card your opponent holds

explanation.surface: Someone boasting about fleecing the person next door at card games.
explanation.walkthrough: Beggar-my-Neighbour is a children's card game in which you aim to take all your opponent's cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living close by shares the same street or district, so is a fellow resident.

clue.text: Music hall -opening for dancing is firm

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of dancing
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A music hall launching a dance programme is a solid venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A discotheque is a hall or club where recorded music is played for people to dance to.

clue.text: Prime supporter of art

parts.note: surface reading: the chief patron or champion of the arts
setter's reading: to prime a canvas is to give it its first coat, and this stand holds the canvas while you paint

explanation.walkthrough: Prime looks like an adjective meaning chief; it is the painter's verb, and the supporter is a literal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's wooden stand holds a canvas upright while it is primed and painted.

clue.text: Dan performed the French number

parts.note: le is French for the
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A performer called Dan doing a number in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Leno was a celebrated Victorian music-hall comedian, so the definition is the man who performed.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the stage name of the Victorian comic Dan who performed in the halls.

clue.text: Circus celebrity has sore back

indicators.note: back here means turned round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star circus performer suffering from a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: The circus is Piccadilly Circus in London, whose famous statue is popularly called by this god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged statue at the heart of Piccadilly Circus is the most famous figure there.

clue.text: Uproar in northern town over a fictitious bear

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, northern England
taken as written
the bear in Kipling's Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A commotion in a northern town about a made-up bear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over means placed above what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a noisy commotion or a fuss with lots of shouting.

clue.text: Man appears to be right with sale-room turnover

parts.note: the verb without its to
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a turnover flips something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market or auction room

explanation.surface: A man seems to be correct about how much an auction house sells.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnover looks like a business word for sales; it reverses the sale-room.
explanation.definitionFit: A male given name stands for a man, as in Bertram Wooster of Wodehouse.

clue.text: Dora set out with a note of anchorage

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A girl called Dora setting off carrying a note to an anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead is a sheltered stretch of water off shore where ships can lie at anchor.

clue.text: Messenger sent for a newspaper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone dispatched to carry letters or packages
second meaning: a common newspaper title, such as the Dundee daily

explanation.surface: Someone sends a runner out to fetch a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the messenger fetching a paper; in fact many papers take the messenger's name as their title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a person who delivers items and is also the name of numerous newspapers.

clue.text: Country mansion let by arrangement in Washington

definitions.note: a place in Washington state, where the answer is a city

parts.note: a country seat is a large house on a rural estate

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country house leased out by agreement in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Let looks like renting out the mansion; here it is just three letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the largest one in Washington State on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Joins forces in French scene of combat

parts.note: en is French for in
the lists were the enclosed ground where knights jousted

explanation.surface: Allies teaming up on a French battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joins forces' suggests an alliance; it means signing up for the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for military service becomes a member of the armed services.

clue.text: Northern Ireland group in charge of river line as adjusted

parts.note: NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland
a lot is a group or batch
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
stray words in the printed clue that supply no letters; they appear to be a printing slip

explanation.surface: A group from Northern Ireland running a river operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue ends with stray words, 'line as adjusted', that play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the Nile, Africa's great river, or the peoples living along it.

clue.text: Churchman rose about five to six, worked with a shovel

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the numbers
in a down clue, rising means going upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
V is the Roman numeral for five
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A clergyman got up early, before six, and did some digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five to six' looks like a time; it is two Roman numerals side by side. A navvy is a manual labourer digging roads or canals.
explanation.definitionFit: To navvy is to do heavy digging work as a labourer, typically with pick and spade.

clue.text: Recognizes, say, the smell of tobacco for instance

definitions.text: the smell of tobacco for instance

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word and take what it sounds like

parts.note: to recognize someone is to know them

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a pipe tobacco by its smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine and tobacco tasters use the word for the aroma or bouquet a product gives off.

clue.text: One in a race in Borrow's Lavengro

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the author's name and the start of the title

explanation.surface: A character in George Borrow's novel Lavengro who belongs to some race or other.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow wrote Lavengro, an 1851 novel about wandering among Gypsies. 'One in a race' suggests a runner; race here is a people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav is a member of one of the peoples of eastern Europe, such as Poles, Czechs or Russians.

clue.text: James I offers. Sydney a spot of leisure

parts.note: James Bond, the fictional spy
taken as written

explanation.surface: James the First presents a moment of rest to someone named Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: Bondi is Sydney's famous surfing beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Australian beach is a place where Sydney residents go to relax and swim.

clue.text: Bereaved widow booked wrongly on a motorway

indicators.note: wrongly means not in the proper order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A grieving widow wrongly charged for driving on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Booked looks like a police charge; it means appearing in a book of the Bible, the Book of Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi loses her husband and both sons, then returns home with her daughter-in-law.

clue.text: A mere reddish pigment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mere is a stretch of still water
second meaning: a crimson dye made from lac or cochineal

explanation.walkthrough: 'A mere' reads as 'only a'; mere is a noun for an inland body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a body of water surrounded by land and a crimson colouring used by painters.

clue.text: Italian city named in sea-trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian city mentioned during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-trip' looks like one noun; trip is the anagram signal working on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a medieval Tuscan hill town known for its Palio horse race.

clue.text: Apparatus of Scotch manufacture destined to be abortive

parts.note: a still is the apparatus used to distil whisky
as in 'born to be king', destined from birth

explanation.surface: Whisky-making equipment doomed to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch is whisky, not anything from Scotland in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes to nothing from the outset is figuratively dead at birth, a failed project.

clue.text: Beautifully got up like a dish at a Borgia feast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wearing glamorous, striking clothes

definitions.text: like a dish at a Borgia feast?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a dressed dish meant to poison, as the Borgias were said to do

explanation.walkthrough: The Borgias, a Renaissance Italian family, were reputed to poison their guests; a dish is dressed with sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in clothes chosen to impress or captivate, glamorous and stunning.
